Do HR and LR share the same co-expression structure? Modules are built inside each group with the
network settings of `01_Processing/06_Module_Building`, then WGCNA's `modulePreservation()` tests each group's modules in the other group's data
(Langfelder et al. 2011).

Two statistics come back per module. Zsummary combines how dense and how connected the module is
in the other group, against permutations: above 10 is strong preservation, 2 to 10 weak to
moderate, below 2 none (Langfelder et al. 2011). The median rank orders modules against each other
and does not depend on module size; lower is better preserved. Each group has 8 people and 24
biopsies, so the test has little power to show a module is missing: Zsummary above 2 says the
module is found again, not that the two networks are the same.

## Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(WGCNA)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
disableWGCNAThreads()
inputs <- c(
  corrected = "01_Processing/03_Blood_Correction/c_data/blood_correction.rds",
  modules = "01_Processing/06_Module_Building/c_data/module_building.rds"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
```

## Input

The blood-corrected matrix that the full-cohort modules were built on, and those modules.

```{r}
#| label: input
corrected <- readRDS(paths[["corrected"]])
modules <- readRDS(paths[["modules"]])
abund <- corrected$E
meta <- modules$meta
stopifnot(identical(colnames(abund), meta$sample_id))
count(meta, group, timepoint)
```

## One network per group

As in `06_Module_Building`, each protein is centred within person, so modules follow within-person
variation. `apply()` over proteins returns biopsies in rows, the orientation WGCNA expects.
A protein with no spread inside one group cannot be correlated there; `goodSamplesGenes()` finds
those, and they are dropped from both groups so the two networks cover the same proteins.

```{r}
#| label: centre
expr <- map(set_names(c("HR", "LR")), \(g) {
  kept <- filter(meta, group == g)
  apply(abund[, kept$sample_id], 1, \(x) x - ave(x, kept$subject))
})
good <- reduce(map(expr, \(x) goodSamplesGenes(x, verbose = 0)$goodGenes), `&`)
expr <- map(expr, \(x) x[, good])
c(dropped = sum(!good), kept = sum(good))
```

`build_group()` builds one group's modules with the `blockwiseModules()` settings and seed of
`06_Module_Building`, and the soft power by the same rule: the WGCNA FAQ's value for a signed
network of that many samples (18 below 20, 16 for 20 to 30, 14 for 30 to 40, 12 above 40). Each
group has 24 biopsies, so both use 16; the scale-free rule would push them to powers where most
proteins fall in no module, as it did for the full network. It returns the power and each protein's
module colour.

```{r}
#| label: build
bicor_args <- list(corType = "bicor", maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = "individual")
build_group <- function(data) {
  power <- c(18L, 16L, 14L, 12L)[findInterval(nrow(data), c(20, 31, 41)) + 1]
  net <- do.call(blockwiseModules, c(
    list(data,
      power = power, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed",
      deepSplit = 2, minModuleSize = 30, mergeCutHeight = 0.15,
      pamStage = TRUE, pamRespectsDendro = TRUE, maxBlockSize = 2500,
      numericLabels = FALSE, randomSeed = 54321, verbose = 0
    ),
    bicor_args
  ))
  list(power = power, colours = set_names(net$colors, colnames(data)))
}
group_modules <- map(expr, build_group)
group_networks <- tibble(
  group = names(group_modules), n_samples = map_int(expr, nrow),
  power = map_int(group_modules, "power"),
  n_modules = map_int(group_modules, \(x) n_distinct(setdiff(x$colours, "grey"))),
  n_unassigned = map_int(group_modules, \(x) sum(x$colours == "grey"))
)
group_networks
```

## Preservation

Each group is the reference once and the test once, with 200 permutations (seeded). `grey`
(unassigned) and `gold` (a random sample WGCNA adds as a baseline) are dropped from the table.

```{r}
#| label: preservation
preservation <- modulePreservation(
  multiData = map(expr, \(data) list(data = data)),
  multiColor = map(group_modules, "colours"),
  referenceNetworks = 1:2, networkType = "signed",
  corFnc = "bicor", corOptions = "maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = 'individual'",
  nPermutations = 200, randomSeed = 42, savePermutedStatistics = FALSE, verbose = 0
)
```

Each group module is labelled with the full-cohort module that holds most of its proteins, so the
two sets of colour names can be read together.

```{r}
#| label: table
full <- set_names(modules$membership$module, modules$membership$uniprot_id)
best_match <- imap(group_modules, \(built, g) {
  tibble(group_module = built$colours, full_module = full[names(built$colours)]) |>
    filter(group_module != "grey") |>
    count(group_module, full_module) |>
    mutate(full_share = n / sum(n), .by = group_module) |>
    slice_max(n, n = 1, by = group_module, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    transmute(reference = g, module = group_module, full_module, full_share)
}) |>
  list_rbind()
preservation_table <- map(c(HR = "LR", LR = "HR"), \(test) {
  reference <- setdiff(c("HR", "LR"), test)
  pair <- c(paste0("ref.", reference), paste0("inColumnsAlsoPresentIn.", test))
  z <- preservation$preservation$Z[[pair]]
  tibble(
    reference = reference, test = test, module = rownames(z), n_proteins = z$moduleSize,
    z_summary = z$Zsummary.pres,
    median_rank = preservation$preservation$observed[[pair]]$medianRank.pres
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(!module %in% c("grey", "gold")) |>
  left_join(best_match, by = c("reference", "module")) |>
  mutate(preservation = cut(z_summary, c(-Inf, 2, 10, Inf),
    labels = c("none", "weak to moderate", "strong")
  ))
count(preservation_table, reference, test, preservation)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-preservation
#| fig-cap: "Zsummary of each group's modules in the other group; dashed: 2 and 10."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
preservation_table |>
  mutate(direction = paste(reference, "modules tested in", test)) |>
  ggplot(aes(n_proteins, z_summary)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(2, 10), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
  geom_point(aes(fill = module), shape = 21, size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = paste0(module, " (", full_module, ")")),
    size = 2.4, seed = 1, colour = "grey25", min.segment.length = 0
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~direction) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "module size (log scale)", y = "Zsummary") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  setequal(preservation_table$reference, c("HR", "LR")),
  !anyNA(preservation_table$z_summary), !anyNA(preservation_table$full_module),
  all(group_networks$n_samples == 24), all(map_lgl(expr, \(x) ncol(x) == sum(good)))
)
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary
preservation_table |>
  summarise(n_modules = n(), min_z = min(z_summary), max_z = max(z_summary), .by = reference)
```

HR builds `r group_networks$n_modules[1]` modules at power `r group_networks$power[1]` and LR
builds `r group_networks$n_modules[2]` at power `r group_networks$power[2]`. Zsummary runs from
`r round(min(preservation_table$z_summary), 1)` to `r round(max(preservation_table$z_summary), 1)`;
`r sum(preservation_table$z_summary < 2)` of `r nrow(preservation_table)` group modules fall
below 2.

## Save

`module_preservation.rds` holds the table and each group's module colours for the figures.

```{r}
#| label: save
out <- here("02_HRvLR", "05_Module_Preservation", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
group_membership <- imap(group_modules, \(x, g) {
  tibble(group = g, uniprot_id = names(x$colours), module = x$colours)
}) |>
  list_rbind()
saveRDS(
  list(
    preservation = preservation_table, group_networks = group_networks,
    group_membership = group_membership
  ),
  file.path(out, "module_preservation.rds")
)
write_workbook(
  list(
    preservation = preservation_table, group_networks = group_networks,
    group_membership = group_membership
  ),
  c(
    "Zsummary and median rank of each group's modules tested in the other group.",
    "Biopsies, soft power, module count and unassigned proteins of each group's network.",
    "Every protein's module in each group's network."
  ),
  file.path(out, "module_preservation.xlsx"), inputs, paths
)
```
